about: The limits of the model a world is measured against, Earth's own figures measured with this model, the rules that give a world its label, and the fixture worlds that pin each rule. A measured bound changes a row here, not code (docs/ARWEN_GLOBAL_WORLDS.md). Read by arwen_global.world.limits.
result_sentence: This is the weather of the first N days after Earth was changed, over a sea surface that does not respond. It is not this world's climate.

skin_temperature_max_k.name: the radiation's surface-temperature range
skin_temperature_max_k.source: RRTMGP k-distribution temperature table, 160 to 355 K; a skin outside it stops the run in the radiation's range gate (core/rrtmgp.py, 'tsfc ... outside the LW temperature range')

air_temperature_min_k.name: the dynamics' research bound on the coldest air
air_temperature_min_k.source: dynamics.py: 'temperature outside research bounds' below 140 K; the radiation radiates air between 120 and 160 K as 160 K (core/rrtmgp.py, cold_floor) and refuses below 120 K

radiation_table_floor_k.name: the radiation tables' coldest temperature
radiation_table_floor_k.source: core/rrtmgp.py cold_floor: colder air radiates as 160 K

surface_pressure_ceiling_pa.name: the radiation's pressure ceiling
surface_pressure_ceiling_pa.source: the radiation accepts layer pressures to 115,000 Pa (core/rrtmgp.py RRTMGP_PLAY_CEILING_PA, da/analysis.py RADIATION_SURFACE_PRESSURE_CEILING_PA); the RRTMGP gas tables end at 109,663.316 Pa and a layer between the two is looked up at the tables' deepest pressure

surface_pressure_floor_pa.name: the floor for taller terrain
surface_pressure_floor_pa.source: the worlds page (docs/ARWEN_GLOBAL_WORLDS.md): taller mountains are refused when the predicted lowest surface pressure is under 450 hPa, until a test moves that number; the vertical grid is proven strictly increasing only down to 500 hPa (vertical.py, HybridCoordinate) and the dynamics refuse under 300 hPa (dynamics.py)

ocean_water_store_kg_m2.name: the water store every column pays its evaporation from
ocean_water_store_kg_m2.source: [initial] surface_water_kg_m2 of the shipped T255 configs; a column that empties stops the run (water.py)

thin_air_surface_pressure_pa.name: the thinnest air the full physics is trusted with
thin_air_surface_pressure_pa.source: docs/arwen-global-worlds-pressure-audit.md: Grell-Freitas holds six live absolute-pressure thresholds and New Tiedtke seven, Morrison none, and the vertical coordinate is checked only down to a 500 hPa surface; the row stays until those thresholds scale with one world-wide factor. The 0.8 bar value itself is a judgment from the worlds page (docs/ARWEN_GLOBAL_WORLDS.md), not a measurement

terrain_scale_max.name: the tallest terrain the [world] table accepts
terrain_scale_max.source: world/spec.py TERRAIN_SCALE_RANGE; the preflight refuses narrower, from the frame

tilt_hot_land_deg.name: the tilt above which a summer continent can reach the skin limit
tilt_hot_land_deg.source: the worlds page (docs/ARWEN_GLOBAL_WORLDS.md): above about 45 degrees with land, a summer continent can pass the radiation's 355 K skin limit within a season (an estimate, not a run)

brightness_plan_low.name: the dimmest sun the plan labels
brightness_plan_low.source: the worlds page (docs/ARWEN_GLOBAL_WORLDS.md): a sun 5 to 10 percent brighter or dimmer

brightness_plan_high.name: the brightest sun the plan labels
brightness_plan_high.source: the worlds page (docs/ARWEN_GLOBAL_WORLDS.md): a sun 5 to 10 percent brighter or dimmer

brightness_min.name: the dimmest sun the [world] table accepts

brightness_max.name: the brightest sun the [world] table accepts

day_length_min_h.name: the shortest day
day_length_min_h.source: world/spec.py DAY_LENGTH_RANGE_H: the stability bound of the rotation term at faster rotation is not measured yet

day_length_max_h.name: the longest day
day_length_max_h.source: world/spec.py DAY_LENGTH_RANGE_H: a slower world waits for the top absorber's setting for slowly rotating worlds

co2_preindustrial_ppm.name: pre-industrial CO2, for the multiples the labels name

co2_glacial_ppm.name: the low end of the CO2 range shown as an illustration (the coldest glacial air)
co2_glacial_ppm.source: the worlds page (docs/ARWEN_GLOBAL_WORLDS.md): CO2 from 180 to 1,120 ppm

co2_illustration_max_ppm.name: the high end of the CO2 range shown as an illustration
co2_illustration_max_ppm.source: the worlds page (docs/ARWEN_GLOBAL_WORLDS.md): CO2 from 180 to 1,120 ppm; from 1,120 to under 10,000 ppm a result must say 'unvalidated above eight times pre-industrial' in full

co2_radiation_max_ppm.name: the largest CO2 the radiation accepts
co2_radiation_max_ppm.source: physics/native_options.py: trace_co2_ppm must lie in (0, 1e4) ppm; world/spec.py CO2_RANGE_PPM

trace_gas_max_ppb.name: the largest methane or nitrous oxide the [world] table accepts

skin_temperature_max_k.source: hottest model skin at T255: 2026-11-11 03Z, 20.36 S 138.28 E, 1-day run from GDAS 2026-11-10 18Z. Not northern summer: no northern-summer T255 output had been written; the T383 run from ERA5 2019-05-20 reached 336.65 K

air_temperature_min_k.source: coldest model air at T255: minimum_temperature_k at hour 72 of the 5-day run from ERA5 2019-01-15 (diagnostics.jsonl); the 10-day run from GDAS 2026-11-10 18Z reached 179.07 K and a T383 10-day run 169.49 K

surface_pressure_min_pa.source: lowest model surface pressure at T255: hour 48 of the 5-day run from ERA5 2019-01-15 (diagnostics.jsonl)

surface_pressure_max_pa.source: highest model surface pressure at T255: hour 144 of the 10-day run from GDAS 2026-11-10 18Z; 107,019 Pa at its step 0 (diagnostics.jsonl)

ocean_store_days.source: days until the first ocean column empties its 500 kg m-2 store on the 0.1.6 line: Gulf of Tehuantepec, 5-day T255 run from ERA5 2019-01-15; 24.8 days in the Persian Gulf from the 10-day run from GDAS 2026-11-10 18Z

request_keys.gravity_m_s2: another gravity (refused by the [world] table: not built yet)
request_keys.radius_km: another planet radius (refused by the [world] table: not built yet)
request_keys.year_length_d: another year length, in Earth days (refused by the [world] table: not built yet)
request_keys.air.composition: another air composition, by name (refused by the [world] table: not built yet)
request_keys.air.surface_pressure_pa: another amount of air, as a global-mean surface pressure (refused by the [world] table)
request_keys.sun.star: another star, by name; 'sun' is Earth's
request_keys.sun.locked: true for a tidally locked planet whose sea answers its sky
request_keys.sea.ocean: a sea that answers the atmosphere ('slab' or 'dynamic'); every world here holds its sea
request_keys.sea.ice_grows: true when sea ice must grow and melt
request_keys.run.climate: true when the result is asked to be the world's climate rather than its first weeks of weather
request_keys.run.regional_zoom: true for a regional ArWen zoom nested in this world
request_keys.run.assimilation: true for cycling, assimilation or an observation scorecard on this world

fact_keys.facts.run_days: the run's length in model days
fact_keys.facts.surface_pressure_min_pa: the lowest surface pressure the preflight predicts for the start
fact_keys.facts.surface_pressure_max_pa: the highest surface pressure the preflight predicts for the start
fact_keys.facts.skin_temperature_max_k: the hottest land skin the preflight predicts for the start
fact_keys.facts.air_temperature_min_k: the coldest air expected during the run
fact_keys.facts.ocean_store_days: days until this world's first ocean column empties its water store (0.1.6 line)

fallback.label: illustration
fallback.limit: a change no row of this table names: shown as an illustration until a row is written for it

rules.label: science
rules.limit: mountains lowered or removed: science for days 2 to 6 near the removed ranges. Days 0 to 2 are the air falling into the space where rock was; after about a week, and anywhere far from the ranges, a difference is shown only where it exceeds the noise floor of a perturbed control

rules.label: illustration
rules.limit: taller mountains: refused when the predicted lowest surface pressure is under 450 hPa, where the model's bottom layer thins

rules.label: not supported yet
rules.limit: terrain more than twice Earth's height is outside the [world] table

rules.label: not supported yet
rules.limit: the terrain is too tall for the model: the predicted lowest surface pressure is under the 450 hPa floor

rules.label: not supported yet
rules.limit: the predicted surface pressure is over the radiation's pressure ceiling

rules.label: not supported yet
rules.limit: the start's land skin, warmed where terrain was removed, is over the radiation's 355 K limit

rules.label: not supported yet
rules.limit: the air is expected colder than the dynamics' 140 K research bound, where the run stops
rules.source: dynamics.py research bound; the worlds page (docs/ARWEN_GLOBAL_WORLDS.md), margin 2

rules.label: not supported yet
rules.limit: the run is longer than the days until the first ocean column empties its 500 kg m-2 water store on the 0.1.6 line, where the run stops; a longer run needs the long-run line
rules.source: the worlds page (docs/ARWEN_GLOBAL_WORLDS.md); the days on Earth are the measured row above

rules.label: illustration
rules.limit: another tilt: correct sun geometry, with ozone and vegetation on Earth's calendar; for the first weeks from an analysis

rules.label: illustration
rules.limit: above about 45 degrees of tilt with land, a summer continent can pass the radiation's 355 K skin limit within a season and the run stops by name

rules.label: illustration
rules.limit: another orbit: the sun's geometry is the world's, everything keyed to the calendar is Earth's

rules.label: illustration
rules.limit: another sun: over a held ocean this is the land and atmosphere's fast adjustment, and a 10-day difference map from one twin is mostly chaos

rules.label: illustration
rules.limit: a sun more than 10 percent brighter or dimmer than the model's: beyond the range the plan labels, unvalidated, and the hottest-skin and coldest-air margins decide whether it runs

rules.label: not supported yet
rules.limit: a sun outside 0.1 to 4 times the model's solar constant is outside the [world] table

rules.label: illustration
rules.limit: another day length: an adjustment from a state balanced for Earth's rotation, not comparable with published equilibrium results that took 1,500 days of spin-up

rules.label: not supported yet
rules.limit: a day shorter than 12 hours waits for the measured stability bound of the model's rotation term

rules.label: not supported yet
rules.limit: a day longer than 100 Earth days waits for the top absorber's setting for slowly rotating worlds, which today damps the day-to-night flow such a world is made of

rules.label: illustration
rules.limit: a waterworld: the prescribed sea temperature largely decides the answer, and no ice can grow or melt

rules.label: illustration
rules.limit: a higher sea: new coastlines under today's weather; the ice sheets whose melting would raise the sea are still there

rules.label: not supported yet
rules.limit: a lower sea uncovers land the edited-Earth surface has no rule to build

rules.label: illustration
rules.limit: another sea surface on Earth's coasts: held for the whole run, so it decides much of the answer

rules.label: illustration
rules.limit: an invented continent: sea temperature, land cover and soil are set by stated rules, and the starting soil wetness the user typed decides the continental interior for more than a month. Good for Earth's air over this map; it is not that world's past or climate, and days 0 to 20 are spin-up
rules.source: the worlds page (docs/ARWEN_GLOBAL_WORLDS.md): a Pangea is an illustration

rules.label: illustration
rules.limit: CO2 held at a number: over a held ocean this is the land and atmosphere's fast adjustment; four times CO2 can warm the troposphere by at most about 0.06 K a day, so a 10-day difference map from one twin is mostly chaos

rules.label: illustration
rules.limit: CO2 below the 180 ppm of the coldest glacial air: below the range the plan labels

rules.label: illustration
rules.limit: CO2 above 1,120 ppm: it runs, and is unvalidated above eight times pre-industrial

rules.label: not supported yet
rules.limit: CO2 at or above 10,000 ppm is outside the radiation's gas range; a runaway greenhouse is outside every scheme
rules.source: physics/native_options.py trace_co2_ppm range; the worlds page (docs/ARWEN_GLOBAL_WORLDS.md)

rules.label: illustration
rules.limit: another trace gas: over a held ocean this is the fast adjustment, and its forcing is a number, not a weather map

rules.label: not supported yet
rules.limit: methane or nitrous oxide at or above 100,000 ppb is outside the [world] table

rules.label: not supported yet
rules.limit: another gravity, radius or air composition, or air thicker than 1.15 bar: the full-physics kernels have Earth's gravity and air compiled in and are pinned by hash, the radiation refuses layers deeper than 1,150 hPa (its gas tables stop at 1,096.6 hPa), and about 240 lines in about 35 files read Earth's constants directly

rules.label: not supported yet
rules.limit: air thinner than about 0.8 bar under the full physics: both carried convection schemes hold live thresholds in absolute pressure that do not scale with the air (docs/arwen-global-worlds-pressure-audit.md), so they would be silently wrong, not refused

rules.label: not supported yet
rules.limit: another amount of air is not supported yet: both carried convection schemes hold live absolute-pressure thresholds that do not scale with the air (docs/arwen-global-worlds-pressure-audit.md)

rules.label: not supported yet
rules.limit: another year length: ozone, vegetation, the land-use season and trace gases are keyed to a 365-day calendar in six places

rules.label: not supported yet
rules.limit: another star: the solar spectrum is fixed and the surface has one broadband albedo

rules.label: not supported yet
rules.limit: a tidally locked planet whose sea is consistent with its sky needs the full physics' own slab ocean, and nobody knows yet whether the dark hemisphere's top levels fall to the 140 K limit

rules.label: not supported yet
rules.limit: a world's own climate: no ocean or sea ice answers the atmosphere, and the one 10-day run on record loses 21.7 W m-2 at the top of the atmosphere; this waits for the slab ocean and thermodynamic sea ice, after the energy deficit is understood

rules.label: not supported yet
rules.limit: ice cannot grow: prescribed thin ice is a heater (61 W m-2 through 1 m of ice with a 30 K difference, physics/frozen_surface.py) and a skin colder than 160 K stops the radiation; snowball and ice-age worlds wait for thermodynamic sea ice

rules.label: not supported yet
rules.limit: a regional ArWen zoom takes terrain, coast and land use from Earth's geography, so on a world with its own coast the storm would sit on modern Earth (world/refusals.py refuses it)

rules.label: not supported yet
rules.limit: assimilation, cycling and observation scorecards compare against Earth's observations and stay refused on any world
